conventions.convention: Wave operators use strong limits of e^{itH} J e^{-itH₀} P_ac(H₀), with separate positive- and negative-time limits; S = Ω₊*Ω₋. Completeness means range equal to H_ac(H), separately from isometry.

Inner products are linear in the first variable and the local resolvent convention is R_T(z) = (T − zI)⁻¹, opposite in sign to the cited general library resolvent definition. Resonances concern specified continued matrix elements and test vectors, not nonreal eigenvalues.

The Gaussian model is dimensionless, g(p) = π⁻³⁄⁴ exp(−|p|²/2), and the continuation uses a disk centered at E₀ > 0 excluding zero, with k(E₀) = √E₀ > 0. The ray defining the entire function starts at w and points horizontally toward positive infinity.

The spatial scattering theorem assumes real bounded compactly supported V on R³, H₀ = −Δ and H on H², Fourier normalization (2π)⁻³⁄², sphere measure 4π, and positive energies only. Resolvent boundary values and generalized adjoints are bounded maps on compact interaction regions.

Finite-channel S is independently specified C¹ data in U(r), r ≥ 1; Q = −iℏS*S′ with ℏ > 0. Basis covariance applies to energy-independent incoming and outgoing unitary matrices. No operational time-measurement interpretation follows from this algebra alone.
The counterexample uses Borel Lebesgue measure on (0,1), rather than its completed sigma-algebra, so the countably generated sigma-algebra hypothesis of the separability supplier applies directly.

load_bearing.statement: A wave operator is complete when its range is all of H_ac(H). When both wave operators exist and are isometries on H_ac(H₀), S = Ω₊*Ω₋; if both are also complete with range H_ac(H), S is unitary. Finite-channel data is separately specified S:I→U(r).

For the specified self-adjoint T, test space X and meromorphic continuation through a real center, a nonreal pole of order k of some continued resolvent matrix element is a resonance matrix-element pole; existence of continuation and identification with an eigenvalue are not asserted.

Assuming AC and Countable Choice, the stated Gaussian matrix element of M_|p|² has continuation m_cont(z) = 2 + 2i√π k(z)e^(−z) ℰ(−ik(z)) on a disk centered at E₀ > 0 excluding zero, with the square-root branch normalized positively at E₀.
For C¹ S:I→U(r) and ℏ > 0, Q = −iℏS*S′ is Hermitian, tr Q = −iℏ(det S)′/det S, and constant incoming/outgoing unitary basis changes give Q♯ = U_in* Q U_in.
